crm_notes:
Account snapshot
- Existing Hosted customer; product team is pushing for Dedicated due to Q4 peak pain (rate-limit spikes + cost unpredictability + ops friction). They are not requesting on-prem; they want predictable performance and clean audit trails.

Why now / key quote(s)
- “We don’t want to buy peak all year. Give us a baseline we can count on, plus a safe way to spike for promos.”
- “When we get denied, we need to know why immediately and what our client should do (retry vs degrade).”

Dedicated + Burst positioning (internal)
- Fit is strong: predictable baseline for real-time copilot traffic; burst for seasonal promos + batch summarization. They are comfortable with shared Redwood-managed burst pools if guardrails protect neighbors and they have visibility/controls.

Proposed configuration (draft / not final)
- Region/hardware: us-east / H100.
- Baseline: sized for normal demand + headroom for typical release week.
- Burst: enabled with a hard cap (monthly) and max burst ratio; cooldown enabled to prevent “perma-burst.”

Operational considerations
- Needs customer-facing dashboards: burst usage over time, current burst headroom, denial reasons breakdown.
- Wants audit events for: enable/disable burst, limit changes, admin overrides.
- They asked whether denials are immediate vs queued. Preference: immediate response with reason codes; they’ll implement backoff + graceful degradation to a smaller model or reduced context.

Risks / watchouts
- Billing sensitivity: they want assurance that retries don’t double-count (they asked for idempotency guidance explicitly).
- Legal: wants exact definitions for “burst pool availability is not reserved capacity” and any SLA language around neighbor protection.

Next actions (owner)
- Lukas/Markus: finalize sizing recommendation + confirm burst cap options for their spend guardrails.
- Michael Grant/Sofia Mendes: provide burst addendum language and confirm how denial semantics are described.
- Miguel (CS): draft cutover + onboarding checklist (dashboards walkthrough, alert recommendations, escalation paths) and schedule a 60-min readiness session.
